transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—I'm Dr. Lee. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Lee. Um… I guess I’m here because I’ve been having a harder time than I’d like to admit staying seated when I’m supposed to. It sounds kind of small, but it’s starting to be noticeable.

Like during client interviews, or tutoring sessions, even at book club, I’ll find myself getting up—just to move around or “do something”—when really I should be sitting and listening. People have started commenting or looking at me, and I don’t want to seem rude or unprofessional. I’m not sure if that’s the kind of thing you help with, but… it’s becoming a problem.
Have you started or changed the dose of any medications—such as antipsychotics, anti-nausea drugs, or antidepressants—around the time this restlessness began?

Um… not that I can think of, no. I mean, I don’t believe there was any medication change around when I started noticing it. I’m not on anything like that as far as I know.

Unless there’s something you’re thinking of that I might not be connecting? But no, nothing stands out to me.
Does this restlessness tend to get worse specifically in the evening or when you're lying down at rest, and does moving your legs relieve it?

I’m not sure I’ve noticed that kind of pattern, honestly. I wouldn’t say it’s especially worse in the evening or when I’m lying down, at least not that I’ve connected.

And it’s not really like my legs feel bad and then moving them fixes it… it’s more just me feeling like I should get up or move. But if that distinction matters, I can pay closer attention.
Along with this urge to move, have you also been feeling unusually worried, on edge, or nervous about things in general?

I don’t think so… not in a general way. I mean, I get concerned about doing a good job or not bothering people, but I wouldn’t say I’m unusually nervous or on edge all the time.

At least, I don’t think that’s the main thing. Does that answer what you’re asking?
Over this same period, have you noticed your mood feeling unusually elevated, euphoric, or irritable, or that you need much less sleep than usual but still feel full of energy?

No, I don’t think so. I haven’t felt euphoric or unusually “up,” and I don’t think I’ve been more irritable than normal.

Sleep-wise, I wouldn’t say I’m needing way less sleep and still feeling energized or anything like that. I mean, I have busy days and I push through, but not in that kind of extreme way, if that makes sense.
Have you noticed any recent unexplained weight loss, a racing heart, excessive sweating, or feeling unusually hot compared to others around you?

No, I don’t think I’ve noticed anything like that. My weight seems about the same, and I haven’t had a racing heart or been sweating a lot for no reason.

I don’t think I run hotter than other people either… at least not that anyone’s pointed out. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Thinking back to when you were a kid, did you tend to be restless, fidgety, or have trouble staying seated in class, or is this something that's really only become noticeable as an adult?

It’s not just an adult thing, no. I mean, I did okay in school, so I don’t want to make it sound like I was a terrible student, but… my grade-school report cards pretty consistently said I was bright, but couldn’t stay in my seat or wait my turn.

My mom still jokes that I treated every classroom like a crime scene I had to pace through. Which is funny, but also probably answers your question, I guess.
Aside from the restlessness, do you often find it hard to stay focused on tasks or conversations, get easily distracted, or frequently lose track of things like keys or deadlines?

I’m not sure, honestly. I mean, everyone loses keys sometimes or gets distracted, right? I don’t want to overstate it.

I do have moments where I have to pull myself back to what someone’s saying, especially if there’s a lot going on around me, but I’ve always kind of thought that was normal. Deadlines… I try to compensate with lists and reminders, so I’m not sure how much counts as a real problem versus just needing to be organized.

Is that the kind of thing you’re asking about?

Would you say these struggles with restlessness and staying focused cause real problems in more than one area of your life—for example, both at work and at home or in relationships—not just in one specific setting?

Yes… I think that’s fair to say. I don’t want to make it sound like I’m falling apart or anything, because I do function, but it’s starting to cost me professionally.

I’ve missed details in investigations that I really should have caught, and I’ve irritated clients by being too… intense, I guess, or jumping ahead. And some of the junior detectives are less willing to debrief with me now because they feel like I steamroll them.

So yes, it’s not just one little setting. It’s affecting work, and I suppose the way people deal with me too. Does that make sense?
Would you say these kinds of restlessness and focus difficulties were already noticeable before you turned 12 years old?

Yes, I think it was definitely there before 12. I mean, I don’t want to make it sound worse than it was—I was considered bright and I did okay—but my grade-school report cards said pretty much every year that I couldn’t stay in my seat or wait my turn.

And my mom still teases me that I treated the classroom like a crime scene I had to pace through, so… yes, I think that was noticeable pretty early.
